title: Extreme observations: score them, investigate them, decide — do not delete them
concepts: z-score vs modified z-score vs IQR
keep / correct / set missing / keep with sensitivity

explain.prompt: The data team proposes to winsorise every price return at the 1st and 99th percentiles “to be safe”. Answer in 5–7 sentences with your decision table: what your investigation found, why the order of the passes matters (give the masking numbers), what you did with the doubtful point and why winsorising would have been wrong.
rubric: 25 observations were examined: 1 unit error corrected (RBOB 14 May 2019 sent in cents: 8,732 $/bbl, exactly ×100 its neighbours), 1 impossible value set missing (gasoil 0.00 on 25 Nov 2021), 11 kept as logged events, 11 kept as market-wide moves confirmed by sister markets, 1 kept as doubtful.

Order matters: with the cents error inside, RBOB's return standard deviation is 0.162 instead of 0.019 and the hurricane day's z-score is only 1.2 — the z-score is masked by the error it should catch; the modified z-score (median/MAD) still gives 12.0. Gross errors first, scores second.

Genuine events are kept: the Gulf Coast hurricane (28 Aug 2017, RBOB +19 %, ULSD +12 % with Brent flat), the 2020 price war and lockdowns, the New York Harbor squeeze (31 Oct 2022, ULSD +20 % while gasoil +3 %). These are exactly the observations a trader studying supply shocks needs.

The doubtful point (jet 15 Jun 2021, +10.8 % with gasoil +2.2 %, no logged event, half reversed the next day) is kept and annotated, with its sensitivity: June 2021 average jet crack 17.32 $/bbl with it, 16.83 without.
Errors had real effects: the unit error alone lifts the 2019 RBOB crack average from 10.1 to 45.0 $/bbl; the zero print moves the November 2021 gasoil crack average from 22.51 to 18.21.

Winsorising at fixed percentiles would have clipped the hurricane, the squeeze and the 2020 collapse (real information) while leaving the cents error at the 1st/99th percentile value instead of correcting it. Outlier detection is not outlier deletion.
